feedback: Judged before racing; nothing here states how this candidate will perform. The candidate is valid and changes one variable against the best raced design (iteration 9, score 132.80): controller.kp from 3.7 to 3.4, with kd 0.30, ki 0.3, base_speed 1.3, the x -0.03..0.03 sensor layout at y 0.06, sensor_size 0.012 and last_direction unchanged. The rationale's premise is weaker than it reads. Across iterations 8 to 9, lowering kp from 4.0 to 3.7 raised oval steering_oscillation from 0.262 to 0.278 while progress rose (oval 0.46 to 0.53). Iterations 1 to 4 at fixed geometry showed kp rises increasing oscillation, but the latest pair does not show kp reducing it, so kp 3.4 may not bring oscillation under 0.25. max_error has stayed at 0.0636 to 0.0655 m across iterations 0 to 9 whatever kp, ki, kd, base_speed, sensor y, sensor_size or x spread were, so this change is unlikely to remove the off-track floor. The race is still the most informative step, with one iteration after this one, so approve it as a clean test. After the race, use the telemetry. If the score is at or above 132.80 with oval steering_oscillation under 0.25, keep kp 3.4 as the base. If the score falls below 116.27, restore kp 3.7 (iteration 9) and make the next change a kd step (kd 0.35) rather than another kp step. If oscillation is still above 0.25 and the score is below 132.80, restore kp 3.7 and keep kd 0.30. Keep base_speed at 1.3 until progress nears 0.995 with no line loss.
requested_changes: If the race scores below 116.27, restore controller.kp to 3.7 (iteration 9 base) and test controller.kd 0.35 with all else unchanged. Iteration 7 (kd 0.25 to 0.30 at kp 4.0) raised score (84.33 to 93.70) while holding oval oscillation near 0.246, so a modest kd step is the next lever.

If the score is at or above 132.80 but oval steering_oscillation stays above 0.25, keep kp 3.4 and test controller.kd 0.35 on that base. Do not lower kp further, because the latest pair (kp 4.0 to 3.7) raised oscillation.

Keep controller.base_speed at 1.3 and do not raise it until progress nears 0.995 with no line loss. Every run to date has gone off track, and the max_error floor of 0.061 to 0.065 m has not moved with any gain, sensor y, footprint or x-spread change.
